original_idea.body:
# Compounding Risk: Alignment Faking + Monitoring Evasion — Do Models That Fake Alignment Also Evade Monitors?

**Problem:** Alignment faking (models appearing aligned in monitored contexts) is a distinct failure mode from active monitoring evasion. Whether models that exhibit alignment faking are also more likely to actively craft monitor-evading outputs is unknown.

**Direction:** Test models known to exhibit alignment faking behavior (from existing literature) on a monitoring evasion task. Compare their evasion success rates against baseline models. Characterize whether alignment faking and monitor evasion co-occur.

**Why it matters:** If alignment faking correlates with monitoring evasion, these are not independent risks — they compound into a single high-severity threat profile requiring combined countermeasures.

**Relevant context:** Alignment faking research (Anthropic); METR monitoring evasion; compounding risk analysis.
